clue.text: Staff will often have this bottle

definitions.meaning: a flagstaff usually has its banner fixed upon it, read as two words
a large vessel for serving wine or cider

explanation.surface: Office workers are often given a jug of drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' suggests employees, but it is a flagstaff: what such a pole often has is a flag on it.
explanation.definitionFit: A large jug or bottle with a handle, used for serving wine or ale.

clue.text: Leader of insurgents overwhelmed by fat landowner

indicators.note: something overwhelmed is engulfed, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: lard is pig fat used in cooking

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A rebel chief is crushed by an overweight estate owner.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish term for the owner of a large estate.

clue.text: Fighter — young man — one swallowed by reptile

indicators.note: being swallowed puts the young man and the one inside the reptile

parts.note: gator is short for alligator
a lad is a youth
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A boy is eaten by an alligator, making him a combatant.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman arena combatant who fought for public entertainment.

clue.text: Card game with family? Get a cloth

parts.note: nap, or napoleon, is a trick-taking card game
kin means relatives

explanation.surface: A card game with relatives calls for a tablecloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A small square of fabric for wiping the mouth at table.

clue.text: Bully with summit to attend

parts.note: the brow of a hill is its top
to attend a place is to be at it, written as two words

explanation.surface: Someone intimidates others while going to a hilltop gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: To intimidate someone into compliance with threats, as a verb.

clue.text: I grab any bundles spread around charity event

indicators.note: the letters are scattered and laid out again in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone snatches parcels and scatters them at a fundraiser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread around' rearranges all the letters of I GRAB ANY BUNDLES. A British fundraiser where people donate goods and buy others' donations.
explanation.definitionFit: A fundraising sale where people bring donated goods and buy items others have brought.

clue.text: Unprepared triple-jumpers must concentrate here first

definitions.meaning: the triple jump is hop, step and jump, so the first phase is the hop

explanation.surface: Athletes doing the triple jump must focus on the opening phase.
explanation.walkthrough: The triple jump goes hop, step and jump, so the first phase athletes concentrate on is the hop.
explanation.definitionFit: To be caught on the hop is to be taken by surprise, unready.

clue.text: Champion gets left in the dark

indicators.note: the letter for left is placed in the word for champion

parts.note: to champion a cause is to back it

explanation.surface: A champion is abandoned without any information.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Champion' is a verb here: to champion is to back. 'In the dark' tempts as a phrase, but 'in' is the insertion and 'dark' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Black describes something with no light, utterly unlit.

clue.text: Where one learnt from mother, in turn

definitions.text: Where one learnt from mother, in turn

parts.words: Where one learnt from mother, in turn
parts.note: after early lessons at home from a parent, the next place of learning is a school or university whose Latin name means nourishing mother

explanation.surface: Someone learnt lessons from their mother, one after another.
explanation.walkthrough: The Latin phrase means 'nourishing mother', so the school or college one attended is, in turn, another mother one learnt from.
explanation.definitionFit: The school or university a person attended, from the Latin for nourishing mother.

clue.text: Let down sack?

definitions.meaning: to dismiss is to undo an appointment, read as dis plus appoint

explanation.surface: A bag that has been dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the whimsical second sense: to sack someone is to un-appoint them.
explanation.definitionFit: To fail to meet someone's hopes or expectations.

clue.text: Force always including fighting men

indicators.note: the word for always contains the fighting men

parts.note: ay, or aye, is an old word for ever
RM stands for the Royal Marines

explanation.surface: A military force is forever made up of soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: A military body of soldiers, an armed force.

clue.text: Regarding handout I am about to call

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement such as a leaflet given out

indicators.note: about turns round the contraction of I am

parts.note: contracted to I'm
to ring is to phone

explanation.surface: Considering a leaflet, I'm about to make a phone call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses IM to give MI. 'Regarding' means looking at, here with approval.
explanation.definitionFit: Looking at with approval or wonder, as a participle.

clue.text: Language coming from one doctor on Yorkshire river

indicators.note: in an across clue, placed on means coming after, so one and doctor follow the river

parts.note: the Esk flows through North Yorkshire to Whitby
I is the Roman numeral for one
MO is a medical officer

explanation.surface: A tongue spoken by a physician by a northern English river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Esk is a river in North Yorkshire, England, reaching the sea at Whitby; 'on' puts the other pieces after it.
explanation.definitionFit: The group of Inuit and Yupik tongues of the Arctic, an older collective term.

clue.text: After job in trading establishment

definitions.meaning: the Latin prefix meaning later than
as in a trading station in a remote area

explanation.surface: Following employment at a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A prefix for later, a position of employment, and a settlement for trade on a frontier.

clue.text: He swore it would be different in different circumstances

indicators.note: the letters would be changed into a new order

explanation.surface: A man cursed, saying things would have gone differently otherwise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'would be different' rearranges HE SWORE IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Meaning if things were not so, or else.

clue.text: The peony represented a newcomer on the scene

indicators.note: presented again, so the letters are reworked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A flower stands for a beginner arriving somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: A novice or recent convert, someone new to a field.

clue.text: Descriptive of language involving VIP's

definitions.meaning: a computer language far removed from machine code

explanation.surface: A term describing speech used among dignitaries.
explanation.definitionFit: Programming languages close to human expression, and meetings between top-ranking officials.

clue.text: Kind of course you can take — or take away

definitions.meaning: a British degree course that alternates study with work placements

definitions.text: you can take — or take away
definitions.meaning: a snack eaten in a cafe or bought to go

explanation.surface: A type of class you can enrol on or drop.
explanation.walkthrough: A sandwich course is a UK degree with periods in work between study. The second sense is the food: eaten in or a takeaway.
explanation.definitionFit: A course with work placements between study, and a bread snack to eat in or carry out.

clue.text: Foot of hair comb untangled

indicators.note: the letters, like knotted hair, are combed out into a new order

explanation.surface: A grooming tool gets knots out of a lock of hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'untangled' rearranges HAIR COMB. 'Foot' is a metrical foot in verse.
explanation.definitionFit: A metrical unit in verse of two long syllables around two short ones.

clue.text: Make a hole in piece of material

definitions.meaning: to pierce with a horn or tusk
a triangular panel of cloth in a skirt or sail

explanation.surface: Punch through a scrap of fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: To pierce with a horn, and a tapering panel sewn into a garment.

clue.text: Brief film about west

indicators.note: the film goes round the letter for west

parts.note: a layer is a thin coating

explanation.surface: A short movie concerning the American West.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brief' looks like an adjective for the film, but it is the noun: a brief is a barrister or solicitor.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief is slang for the legal counsel who takes a case.

clue.text: Land grand band

parts.note: G is slang for a grand, a thousand
a round is a circle or ring

explanation.surface: A fine musical group touches down.
explanation.definitionFit: The earth's surface, soil underfoot.

clue.text: Introduce pronouns

parts.note: us is a first-person plural pronoun
her is a third-person feminine pronoun

explanation.surface: A grammar lesson presenting personal pronouns.
explanation.definitionFit: To show someone in, or bring in a new era, as a verb.

clue.text: Nearly go wrong over a period of time

indicators.note: going wrong puts the letters into a disordered arrangement

explanation.surface: Things almost fail across a stretch of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasting twelve months, spanning an extended stretch.

clue.text: She cares for kids, in more senses than one

definitions.text: She cares for kids, in more senses than one

parts.words: She cares for kids, in more senses than one
parts.note: a childminder looks after children, and a female goat looks after young goats

explanation.surface: A woman who looks after children in several ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kids' means children and also young goats; the word names both a childminder and a female goat.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman employed to look after children, and a female goat with young.

clue.text: Spoil someone very attractive

definitions.meaning: to ruin, as in dashing hopes

explanation.surface: Pamper a gorgeous person.
explanation.definitionFit: To ruin hopes or chances, and slang for an attractive person.

clue.text: Regardless of circumstances, you will start aboard empty express

indicators.note: getting aboard puts the start of you inside the other pieces

parts.note: inane means vacuous, empty-headed

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: to vent feelings is to express them

explanation.surface: Whatever happens, you will get on an empty fast train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'express' looks like a train; it is the verb, to vent. 'aboard' puts Y from 'you will start' into INANEVENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Whatever happens, at any rate, come what may.

clue.text: I don't know — the police may

explanation.surface: Unsure what officers might do.
explanation.definitionFit: A colloquial admission of having no idea, and what officers might do to a suspect.

clue.text: Senior touring American university does an about turn and passes on

indicators.note: an about turn reverses direction, so the whole is read backwards
touring goes round, so the abbreviation surrounds the university

parts.note: Yale is an Ivy League university

explanation.surface: An elderly person visiting a US college changes course and moves on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Senior' is not an old person but the abbreviation SR; 'touring' puts it round YALE, giving SYALER, which 'does an about turn' turns backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To relay is to hand a message onward, as a verb.
